method.step: Open the can of mandarin oranges, and drain the liquid into a large bowl. Transfer ¼ cup of the liquid into a small bowl, and set aside. Season the chicken with salt, and add it to the mandarin liquid in the large bowl. Toss to coat and set aside.
Add the honey, lemon juice, soy sauce, ginger, and cornstarch to the reserved ¼ cup of mandarin liquid, and whisk until the cornstarch dissolves. Set aside.

Heat a large nonstick pan over medium heat, and lightly coat with the olive oil spray. Add the chicken and any remaining marinade to the pan, and cook for about 5 minutes, until all sides of the chicken are brown.

Stir in the honey mixture, and bring to a gentle simmer. Simmer for about 4 minutes, until the sauce has thickened and the chicken is cooked through. Add in the orange zest, crushed red pepper (if using), and mandarin oranges. Cook for about 1 minute, until the mandarin oranges are heated through. Remove from the heat.
Divide among four plates, garnish with more soy sauce, or crushed red pepper if you prefer, and serve.
In a large pot over medium heat, heat the coconut oil. Add the curry powder and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the onion, ginger, and garlic, and cook, stirring often, reducing the heat if necessary to prevent browning, until softened, about 4 minutes.
Increase the heat to medium, and add the eggplant and lemongrass paste. Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 5 minutes, until the vegetables are just beginning to soften.

Add the coconut milk and enough water to cover the eggplant, and bring to a simmer. Add the chicken, and simmer very gently for about 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through. Season with salt or curry powder for extra flavor.

While the curry is cooking, prepare the cauliflower. To rice the cauliflower, remove the stem and chop the head into small florets. Using a food processor, blender, or grater, process the cauliflower into pieces the size of rice. Put the riced cauliflower in a microwave- safe bowl, cover, and microwave on high for 3 minutes, or until the cauliflower is tender. A larger head of cauliflower will need more time to cook.
Divide the cauliflower rice and curry among four plates, squeeze one lime quarter over each, sprinkle with cilantro, and serve.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Cut the orange in half. From the center of the orange, cut three rounds about ¼ inch thick from one of the halves. Lay the rounds in a row in a small baking dish with a cover.
Place the chicken breast over the orange rounds, and squeeze the juice from the remaining orange half over the chicken breast. Add the water, pouring around, but not on, the chicken.

Carefully tear open the packet of chai, and lightly dust the top of the chicken breast with some of its contents. You do not have to use all of the contents. More will give a stronger taste. Season with salt.
Cover the dish, and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove from the oven, and let it rest, covered, for 10 minutes before serving.
In a large nonstick saucepan over medium-high heat, heat the coconut oil. Add the chicken, garlic, and salt, and cook for about 5 minutes, until the chicken browns.
Stir in the mushrooms and lemongrass paste, and cook for about 5 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender.
Stir in the cayenne, coconut milk, water, cilantro, and lime juice. Bring to a simmer, and continue cooking for 10 more minutes.
Divide among four bowls and serve. If you prefer, garnish with more cilantro and lime juice.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
In the bottom of a large baking pan with a cover, place the onion slices in a thin layer.
Fillet each chicken breast horizontally and open as you would a book. Spread the roasted garlic evenly among the breasts, and close them back up so that the cloves are layered inside each breast.

Place the chicken over the onion in the pan, and season each breast with salt, black pepper, and crushed red pepper. Spread the nutritional yeast evenly over the breasts, and then spoon the crushed tomatoes over all, gently spreading it with the back of a spoon to evenly coat each breast. Sprinkle the Italian seasoning, basil, and mozzarella (if using) on top.
Cover and bake the chicken for 20 minutes. Remove the cover, and bake for 10 minutes more, until the center is no longer pink.
Remove from the oven and let rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.

Using a knife, remove the cabbage’s core. Place the cabbage in a microwave- safe bowl. Add the water, and cover with plastic wrap, making a slit to vent. Microwave on high for 12 minutes, or until the leaves are tender and peel away easily.

While the cabbage is steaming, heat a medium nonstick skillet over medium- high heat, and add the ground turkey. Sprinkle the turkey with the pepper, salt, and basil. Cook until the turkey has browned, about 8 minutes. Drain off any liquid.
Add the onion and garlic, and cook for about 5 minutes more, until the onion is translucent.
Add the spinach, and cook for about 2 minutes, until the spinach is wilted. Stir in the nutritional yeast, remove from heat, and set aside to cool.
In a small bowl, mix together the crushed tomatoes and tomato sauce. Spread half of the mixture in the bottom of a 9-by-13-inch baking dish, and reserve the other half.
When the cabbage is cool enough to handle, gently peel off 10 whole leaves one by one.

Lay one leaf down cup-side up with the stem facing you. Place ⅓ cup of the turkey mixture in the center of the leaf. Fold the stem end over the mixture, then fold the sides toward the center, then roll the package away from you. Place each roll, stem-side down, in the baking dish. Repeat with the remaining cabbage leaves and turkey filling. When all the cabbage rolls are done, pour the remaining tomato mixture evenly over the top.
Cover the dish with foil, bake for 90 minutes, and serve.
In a small bowl, mix well to combine the coffee, garlic, salt, black pepper, cayenne pepper, cinnamon, and cloves.
Store in a sealed storage container.
In a small bowl, mix the olive oil, garlic, apple cider vinegar, balsamic, soy sauce, mustard, cloves, and pepper until well combined.
Carefully transfer the marinade to a 1-gallon resealable bag, and add the steaks. Massage the bag to ensure the steaks are well coated.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat the grill or a large cast iron pan on the stove to high heat.
Grill for 7 to 15 minutes, depending on the thickness of the steak and your preferred doneness.
Let the steak rest for 5 to  10 minutes before carving against  the grain and serving.
In a small bowl, stir the rosemary, garlic, crushed red pepper, and olive oil into a loose paste.
Spread the mixture evenly over the steaks, and season with salt (if using).
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. Ensure the grill is clean.
Place the steaks on the hottest part of the grill, and quickly sear both sides until they are brown, less than 2 minutes per side.
Move the steaks to a cooler part of the grill, and cook to desired doneness, about 5 to 6 more minutes per side.
Remove the steaks from the grill, and let rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
Cut the steak off the bone, slice across the grain, and serve.
Preheat the oven to 300°F.
Line a baking sheet with nonstick aluminum foil.
Pat the steak surfaces dry, and sprinkle each side with a pinch of salt (if using).
In a large skillet over high heat, heat the coconut oil until you see gentle smoke lifting off of the surface.
Using tongs, place the steak in the skillet, and sear for 1 minute on each side.
Place the steaks in the prepared baking sheet, and bake for 20 to 30 minutes, checking often to make sure the steak does not overcook. This steak is best served rare to medium rare.
Remove from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes.
Carve against the grain in thin slices and serve.
Warm a large pot over medium-high heat. Heat ¾ teaspoon of olive oil, and add the beef. Cook until all sides are brown, about 5 minutes. Remove from the pot, and set aside.
Add the remaining ¾ teaspoon of olive oil to the pot, followed by the celery and onion, and cook for 10 minutes.

Add the browned beef, tomato juice, broth, carrots, potatoes, diced tomatoes, bay leaves, corn, and garlic to the pot, and stir to combine. Bring to a boil. Reduce the heat, and simmer uncovered for 1 hour.
Add the peas and hot sauce to the soup, cover, and simmer for about 30 minutes longer.
Remove the bay leaves, ladle into bowls, and serve.
Heat a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef, bell pepper, and onion, and cook for about 5 minutes, until browned. Drain off any grease, if necessary.
Add the garlic, red beans, kidney beans, tomatoes, chili powder, cumin, oregano, and salsa, and cook for 7 to 10 minutes more, until heated through, stirring frequently.
Ladle into bowls and serve.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef and onions, and cook for about 5 minutes, until brown. Drain off any grease, if necessary.

While the beef is browning, in a small bowl, stir to combine the tomato sauce, tomato paste, apple cider vinegar, honey, stevia, soy sauce, mustard powder, cinnamon, and pepper until well blended. Set the sauce aside.
Add the red pepper, green pepper, garlic, and jalapeño (if using) to the beef, and cook for about 5 minutes more, stirring often.
Stir in the prepared sauce. Reduce the heat, simmer for about 5 minutes, and serve.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.

In a large bowl, mix lightly but thoroughly to combine the beef, tomato juice, apple, oats, egg, onion, parsley, salt (if using), pepper, allspice, and mustard powder. Do not overmix or you will end up with a tough meatloaf. Press the mixture into an 8-by-4-inch loaf pan, and bake for 1 hour.
Remove from the oven and let sit for about 15 minutes.
Slice into four even pieces and serve. If there are any leftovers, this loaf tastes even better the next day.
Preheat the oven to 275°F.

In a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat, heat 1½ teaspoons of olive oil. Add the onions and carrots, and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until lightly brown. Remove the onions and carrots from the pot, and set aside.

Generously season the chuck roast with pepper. Add the remaining 1½ teaspoons of olive oil to the pot, and increase the heat to high. Place the roast in the pot, and sear it for 1 minute on each side, until brown. Transfer the roast to a plate.

With the burner still on high, add 1 cup of broth to the pot and deglaze, using a spoon to scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Place the roast back in the pot, and add enough stock to come halfway up the meat. Add the onions and carrots, spreading them around the roast. Loosely sprinkle the rosemary and thyme on top of the roast.
Cover the pot, transfer to the oven, and roast for 3 hours.
The roast is ready to serve when the meat is tender and falls apart easily. ≈
In the slow cooker, stir to combine the roast, broth, tomatoes, carrots, potatoes, onion, celery, soy sauce, apple cider vinegar, parsley, oregano, pepper, and garlic. Cook on high for 6 hours.
About 30 minutes before it is done cooking, in a small bowl, mix the water and cornstarch together, and pour the mixture into the slow cooker. Mix well, and cook for the remaining 30 minutes.
Skim the top of your stew to remove and discard as much of the fat as you can, ladle the stew into bowls, and serve.
Preheat the oven to 500°F.
Season the roast with the salt, pepper, garlic, thyme, and rosemary. Place in a foil-lined roasting pan or baking dish for easy cleanup. Do not cover or add water.

Place the roast in the oven, and immediately reduce the temperature to 475°F. From now until the end of cooking, do not open the oven door until the roast is completely done. Doing so will allow precious heat to escape, and the roast may not cook all the way through.
After 21 minutes (larger roasts will need more time; allow for 7 minutes more per extra pound), turn off the oven and allow the meat to continue roasting for 2½ hours.
Remove the roast from the oven, and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Carve into thin slices against the grain and serve.

Put the steak, onions, broth, apple cider vinegar, lime juice, olive oil, garlic, salt, coriander, cumin, paprika, and oregano in a large resealable bag. Massage to ensure the meat is well coated. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.

Pour the contents of the bag into a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender.
Serve.

recipes.title: SALISBURY STEAK WITH MUSHROOM AND ONION GRAVY
recipes.author: Kendall Lou Schmidt

method.step: In a large bowl, mix to combine the beef, egg, garlic, onion, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper, and thyme. Using your hands, form eight oval patties of equal size.
In a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat or on a grill, cook the patties for 3 to 5 minutes per side. Cooking time will vary depending on thickness and desired doneness.

In a large skillet over medium-high, heat the olive oil. Add the onion, garlic, and mushrooms and cook for about 7 minutes, until the onion becomes translucent and slightly browned, stirring frequently.

In a small bowl, stir together 2 tablespoons of broth and the cornstarch. When the cornstarch has dissolved, stir in the remaining broth, and add the liquid to the skillet. Stir until slightly thickened, and then add the pepper, salt, garlic powder, and onion powder. Cook for an additional 5 minutes, stirring frequently. Remove from the heat.
Place one hamburger steak on each plate, top with a generous scoop of mushroom-onion gravy, and serve.
In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, apple cider vinegar, lemon juice, garlic, hot sauce, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Reserve half the marinade in a separate bowl. Cover and refrigerate until later.

Add the beef cubes to a large resealable bag. Add the remaining marinade, and massage the bag to ensure all the beef is well coated. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours and up to overnight.

Preheat the grill to medium-high. Ensure the grill is clean. Lightly oil the grill. Alternatively, preheat the oven broiler to high, set the rack about 8 inches from the heat, and line a broiler pan with aluminum foil.
Thread the beef cubes and onion pieces onto 12 skewers, alternating the beef and onion. Grill for 3 to 4 minutes on each side for medium-rare.
Place the kebabs on a serving platter, and drizzle with the reserved marinade, or remove the skewers, place the meat in your meal prep containers, and drizzle with the reserved marinade.
Preheat the oven to 375 °F.
In a large pan over medium-high, heat the olive oil. Add the kale, onion, and garlic, and cook until the onion softens, about 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the green onion and bell pepper, and cook for 5 minutes more, stirring frequently. Remove the mixture from the pan, and set aside.
Add the ground beef to the pan, and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until cooked through.

Add the kale, onion, and pepper mixture back into the pan along with the tomatoes, parsley, Italian seasoning, and seasoning salt, and mix well. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until warmed through. Remove from the heat.
Fill each of the hollow green peppers with one-quarter of the stuffing. Pour the reserved tomato liquid into a baking dish, and place the peppers in the dish on the tomato liquid.
In a small bowl, stir together the tomato paste, garlic, oregano, and basil. Top each stuffed pepper with one- quarter of the mixture, and sprinkle each pepper with 1 tablespoon of the mozzarella.
Bake in the oven for 20 minutes, or until the cheese is golden brown, and serve.

Put the beef, orange juice, rice vinegar, soy sauce, hot chili paste, stevia, and garlic in a resealable bag. Massage the bag to ensure the meat is well coated. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.

Over a small bowl, use scissors to cut one of the bottom corners off the resealable bag, and squeeze all the marinade from the bag into the bowl. Add the water and cornstarch to the marinade, and whisk until the cornstarch is dissolved. Set aside.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over high heat, and lightly coat with olive oil spray. Add the beef, and cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the white parts of the green onions and the orange zest, and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the marinade and the remaining green onions, season with salt and pepper, and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until the beef is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Divide among four plates and serve.

On a work surface, using a sharp knife, trim the pork of all but a ¼-inch layer of fat. In a large bowl, rub the pork all over with the olive oil. Sprinkle with the salt, oregano, cumin, and pepper, and rub to coat.
Place the pork in a slow cooker or a rice cooker with a slow cook setting with the fat side facing up. Sprinkle with the onion, jalapeño, and garlic.
Squeeze the juice from the oranges over the pork, and sprinkle the grated peel over the top.
Cook on high for about 5 hours. The pork is done when it is tender and breaks apart with very little effort.

Transfer the pork from the slow cooker to a platter, let rest for 5 to 10 minutes, and then shred the pork using two forks. Skim off and discard the fat from the juices. Refrigerate the juices for when reheating pork.

Heat a large pan over high heat for 1 minute, and lightly coat with the olive oil spray. Add the amount of shredded pork you’re ready to serve, press down with a spatula, and cook until the bottom side is golden brown. Leave the top side as is, and serve. To freeze: Pack the pulled pork in airtight containers, portioning 1 week’s worth of meal prep in each container (this will allow you to defrost only what is needed when the time comes). Distribute the juices from the slow cooker evenly among the containers.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Place the pork tenderloin in a large bowl. Add the balsamic vinegar, and turn to coat. Let it marinate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, mix the mustard with the garlic, dried onion, pepper, rosemary, thyme, and dill. It will form a very thick paste.
Place the tenderloin on a foil-lined baking sheet, and pour the balsamic on top.
Using your hands, press the paste in an even layer onto the top and sides of the tenderloin. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes.
Remove from the oven and let rest on the baking sheet for 10 minutes.
Transfer to a cutting board, slice the tenderloin against the grain into six equal pieces, and serve.
In a blender or food processor, blend the soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, and ginger until smooth.

Place the pork in a dish not much larger than the roast itself. Pour the marinade over the pork, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for 4 hours. Remove the roast from the refrigerator 1 hour prior to roasting.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
In a foil-lined baking dish, roast the pork for 20 to 25 minutes, until cooked through. Cooking time will vary based on thickness and diameter.
Remove from the oven and let rest for 10 minutes before carving and serving.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.

In a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat, heat the coconut oil. Add the minced garlic, and cook, stirring, for 1 minute. Add the tenderloin, and cook, turning a few times, until lightly seared all around, about 5 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to the oven, and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, turning over once halfway through cooking time, until cooked through. Cooking time will vary depending on the thickness of the meat.
Immediately drizzle the honey over the entire length of the tenderloin, and let rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
Using a sharp knife, slice the tenderloin against the grain into six equal pieces. Serve warm.
In a shallow bowl, lightly beat the egg.
In a separate shallow bowl, mix the almond flour with the Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Coat the pork chops in the egg, and then dredge the egg-coated pork in the almond flour mixture. Shake to remove any excess.
In a medium skillet over medium- high heat, heat the olive oil. Add the pork chops and cook, turning once, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes per side.
Transfer to plates and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
In a large, deep soup pot over medium-high heat, heat the olive oil.
Add the carrots, celery, and onion, and cook covered, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the beans, chicken broth, ham, chili powder, bay leaf, garlic, and pepper, and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat down to low, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Discard the bay leaf, ladle into soup bowls, and serve hot.
On a work surface, pat the tenderloin dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, slice the tenderloin against the grain into ½-inch-thick slices, and cut the slices into ½-inch strips.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. If needed, coat very lightly with olive oil. Add the pork and ginger, and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the water with the stevia and cornstarch until the cornstarch has dissolved. Add the slurry to the pork, and stir to coat.
Add the baby bok choy, carrots, and red and green bell peppers to the skillet. Cover and cook for about 5 minutes, until the vegetables begin to soften.
Add the soy sauce, lemon zest, and lemon juice to the skillet. Cook, uncovered, stirring frequently, for 2 to 5 minutes more, until all of the vegetables are tender.
Divide the pork and vegetables among four plates, and serve.
In a slow cooker or a rice cooker with a slow cook setting, stir well to mix the pork, broth, cilantro, Anaheim chiles, jalapeños, onion, garlic, salt, cumin, black pepper, oregano, and cloves.
Cook on high for 6 hours.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot, with the lime wedges alongside. If you like, serve with a dollop of yogurt and a few cubes of chopped avocado (remember to add the calories to the total).
On a work surface, pat the tenderloin dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, cut the tenderloin against the grain into 1-inch-thick slices, and cut the slices into 1-inch cubes.
Tenderize the pork by piercing each cube with a fork in a few places.
In a small bowl, mix the reserved pineapple juice and vinegar with the garlic powder, ginger, and cayenne.
Put the cubed pork in a large resealable bag, add the marinade, seal the bag, and massage to coat the pork evenly. Marinate in the refrigerator for 15 minutes.

Thread the pork, pineapple chunks, bell peppers, onion, and tomatoes onto 10 skewers, alternating among the vegetables. For the sake of portions, spread the pork and pineapple evenly among the skewers, so that each skewer holds about 4 ounces of pork and 2 ounces of pineapple.
Preheat a grill to medium. Alternatively, preheat the oven broiler to high heat, set the rack about 8 inches from the heat, and line a broiler pan with aluminum foil.
Grill or broil the skewers, turning a few times, until the pork is lightly charred and cooked through, 8 to 12 minutes.
Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
In a small bowl, mix the fennel seeds, sage, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper, parsley, and salt together to make a rub.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil or a silicone baking mat.
Pat the tenderloin dry with paper towels. Sprinkle the tenderloin with the rub, and massage well to coat. Set the tenderloin on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once halfway through, until cooked through.
Transfer the pork to a cutting board and let rest for 10 minutes.
Using a sharp knife, slice the tenderloin against the grain into six equal portions.
Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
In a small bowl, mix the coffee, cayenne, and salt together to make a rub.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil or a silicone baking mat.
Pat the tenderloin dry with paper towels. Sprinkle the tenderloin with the rub, and massage well to coat. Place the tenderloin on the prepared baking sheet.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once halfway through, until cooked through.
Transfer to a cutting board and let rest for 10 minutes.
Using a sharp knife, slice the tenderloin against the grain into six equal portions, and transfer to a platter.
Drizzle the balsamic vinegar over the length of the sliced tenderloin, and serve immediately.

Put the shrimp, olive oil, lime juice, garlic, stevia, paprika, Italian seasoning, and basil in a large resealable bag. Massage the bag to ensure the shrimp are well coated. Marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Thread the shrimp onto skewers. If you are not using a rack, be sure to lightly spray the surface they are cooking on to prevent them from sticking.
To grill: Allow the barbecue to warm up to medium heat before placing the shrimp on the grill.

To broil: Set the oven rack about 8 inches from the broiler, line a broiler pan with aluminum foil, and arrange the shrimp skewers on it. Set your broiler to high and allow the oven to heat up a bit before placing the shrimp in it.
Cook the shrimp for 8 to 10 minutes, turning over once after 4 to 5 minutes. They are done when opaque with pink tails.
Serve warm.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat the olive oil. Add the celery, onion, and garlic, and cook until tender, but not brown, about 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato sauce, soy sauce, apple cider vinegar, lemon juice, stevia, salt, and chili powder. Simmer uncovered for at least 20 minutes, and up to 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In a small bowl, mix the cornstarch and water. Stir the mixture into the skillet, and cook until the sauce is thick and bubbly.
Add the bell pepper and shrimp, cover, and simmer for 5 minutes more.
Divide among four bowls and enjoy.

recipes.title: COCONUT SHRIMP WITH SWEET AND SPICY DIPPING SAUCE
recipes.author: Kendall Lou Schmidt

method.step: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Put the cornstarch in a small bowl.
In a second small bowl, whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form.
In a third small bowl, mix the coconut and stevia.

Set the three bowls in a row. Take one shrimp by the tail, coat it in cornstarch, and then dip it in the whipped egg whites, the more volume the better. Finally, coat the shrimp in the coconut, and place it on the baking sheet.
Bake at 375°F for 10 to 15 minutes, turning over after about 7 minutes. The shrimp are done when the coconut has toasted and the tails are pink. (The egg white, if exposed, will still be white.)
While the shrimp are in the oven, in a small bowl, mix the marmalade with the sriracha. If necessary, add a little water, 1 teaspoon at a time, to thin out the dipping sauce as needed.
Serve the shrimp warm with the dipping sauce.
In a large bowl, mix together the honey, soy sauce, garlic, and ginger. Transfer half of the mixture to another small bowl, and set aside.
Add the shrimp to the sauce in the large bowl, and toss to coat well. Marinate in the refrigerator for 15 minutes.

In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat the coconut oil. Drain and discard any excess marinade from the shrimp, add the shrimp to the hot oil, and sear on both sides, about 1 minute per side, until the shrimp have slightly browned and the tails are pink. Remove from the heat.
Using a fork or tongs, rub the shrimp against the bottom of the skillet to collect the caramelized honey on the bottom of the pan.
Transfer to a plate, and drizzle with the remaining sauce. Divide among four plates and serve.
Place a large pot of water over high heat. Bring to a boil.

Put the shrimp in the boiling water for 45 seconds. Quickly pour the contents of the pot over a strainer in the sink, and then immediately transfer the shrimp to ice-cold water; this stops the cooking. Drain when cooled.
Chop the shrimp into ½-inch pieces and put them in a large bowl.
Pour the lime juice, lemon juice, orange juice, and grapefruit juice over the shrimp, and toss to coat.
Add the tomatoes, red onion, cilantro, and jalapeño, and toss gently. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 4 hours.
Add the cucumbers and avocados before serving.
In a large soup pot over medium heat, heat the olive oil. Add the fennel, onion, shallots, and salt (if using), and cook for 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until the onion is translucent.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes, and cook for 2 minutes more.

Stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes with their juices, fish stock, lemon juice, water, and bay leaf. Cover and bring to a simmer, and then reduce the heat to medium-low. Continue to simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the clams and mussels, cover, and cook for about 5 minutes, until the clams and mussels begin to open.

Add the shrimp and fish, and cook for about 5 minutes more, until the fish and shrimp are cooked through and the clams and mussels are completely open. Stir gently, careful not to break apart the fish.
Discard the bay leaf and any clams and mussels that failed to open.
Ladle a little of each shellfish, a little mahimahi, and some soup into each bowl, season with more salt and red pepper flakes as desired, and serve.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the coconut oil, and swirl the skillet to coat the bottom.
Fill the skillet with spinach leaves. Cook, stirring, until wilted, about a minute. Add more spinach to the skillet, and repeat the process until all of the spinach is wilted.
Transfer the spinach to a plate, and lightly dust with nutmeg.
Return the skillet to medium-high heat, add the coconut oil, and swirl to coat the bottom.

On a work surface, pat the scallops dry with paper towels, season with salt, and add to the skillet. Cook undisturbed for 1 to 2 minutes, until the bottoms brown. Flip, season with salt, and cook for another 1 to 2 minutes. They will be browned on both sides and cooked through but still slightly pink in the center.
Place the scallops atop the wilted spinach and enjoy.
In a small bowl, mix well to combine the soy sauce, lemon juice, rice vinegar, honey, cornstarch, apple cider vinegar, garlic, and pepper.
Pat the scallops dry with paper towels. In a medium bowl, drizzle the scallops with less than half of the marinade. Toss to coat.
Heat a large skillet over medium- high heat. Add the oil, and swirl to coat the pan. Add the scallops, and sear for 1 minute on each side. Remove and set aside.

Add the bok choy, mushrooms, snow peas, bell peppers, and onion to the skillet, and cook for about 5 minutes, until tender. Add the remaining marinade, and cook until heated through. Add the scallops back into the skillet, and cook for 1 more minute.
Divide among four plates and serve.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Place the scallops on a foil-lined baking sheet 1½ inches apart.
In a small bowl, mix the mustard and maple syrup. Spoon the mixture evenly over the scallops, and spread to coat the top.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, depending on size, until opaque.
Enjoy warm.
In a small bowl, use a fork to mix the tuna, onion, pickle, yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, dill, and pepper until well combined.
Drizzle the balsamic vinegar over the top and enjoy.
Preheat the broiler to high. In a small bowl, use a fork to mix the tuna, yogurt, basil, bell pepper, onion, and black pepper until well blended.
Slice off the top of each tomato with a sharp knife, and use a spoon to hollow out the tomatoes.
Stuff the tuna mixture into the tomato cups, and press down firmly with a fork.
Place the stuffed tomatoes in a loaf pan or baking dish. Top each with 2 tablespoons of shredded mozzarella and a pinch of crushed red pepper.
Broil 6 to 8 inches from the heat for 3 to 5 minutes, until the cheese melts and slightly browns.
Serve immediately. The stuffed tomatoes go well with salad greens or a veggie side dish. 1 stuffed  tomato
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Line a baking sheet with nonstick aluminum foil or a silicone baking mat.
In a medium bowl, whisk the egg and egg whites. Set aside.
In a large bowl, mix together the almond flour, mustard, cayenne pepper, and garlic powder.

On a work surface, pat the cod dry with paper towels. Dip a cod fillet into the egg, coating both sides. Shake off any excess. Dredge in the almond flour mixture, coating both sides, and place the seasoned cod on the prepared baking sheet. Repeat with the remaining cod.
Lightly spray each breaded fillet with olive oil spray. Bake for 15 minutes.
Plate the fish and serve fresh from the oven. 1 6-ounce   cod fillet
In a large bowl, stir together the salmon and its liquid with the quinoa. Add the beet, onion, garlic, and parsley, and mix well.
In a medium bowl, use a fork to beat the egg, egg whites, yogurt, nutritional yeast, and salt together.
Add the egg mixture to the salmon and quinoa mixture, and stir until well combined. 3 cakes
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the oil, and swirl to coat.

Using a ¼-cup measuring cup, scoop as many cakes into the skillet as will fit without the edges touching. Do not overcrowd. Fry for 5 to 8 minutes, until the bottoms brown and the cakes are firm. Flip and brown the other side, 3 to 5 minutes more.
Transfer to a dish to keep warm, and continue frying until all of the mixture has been used. The batter should make close to 18 cakes.
Serve warm.

recipes.title: GRILLED CALAMARI STEAKS WITH MEDITERRANEAN TOPPING
recipes.author: Kendall Lou Schmidt

method.step: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, stir together the olives, tomatoes, capers, parsley, lemon zest and juice, garlic, and pepper.
In a medium bowl, cover the calamari steaks with the lemon juice, olive oil, and parsley. Season with salt and pepper, and toss to combine.
Place the steaks directly over the heat on the grill. Grill the steaks for about 2 minutes on each side, until opaque. Do not overcook, or the calamari will be tough.
Top each calamari steak with half of the olive topping and a squeeze of lemon juice from the wedges, and serve.
In a small bowl, use a fork to stir the nutritional yeast, olive oil, dried basil, and salt into a paste. The paste will be grainy.
TO COOK IN THE OVEN, step 1: Preheat the oven to 350°F.

TO COOK IN THE OVEN, step 2: Place the fillets on a baking sheet lined with nonstick aluminum foil or on a silicone baking sheet. Spread the paste over the tops of each fillet, pressing it down into place.
TO COOK IN THE OVEN, step 3: Bake for 15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily when tested with a fork, and serve.
TO COOK IN THE MICROWAVE, step 1: Place the fillets on a microwave-safe dish. Spread the paste over the tops of each fillet, pressing it down into place.
TO COOK IN THE MICROWAVE, step 2: Microwave on high for 4 to 5 minutes, depending on the size of the fillets, until the fish flakes easily when tested with a fork.
TO COOK IN THE MICROWAVE, step 3: Allow them to rest for 1 to 2 minutes before serving.

method.step: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
In a small nonstick pan over medium-high heat, cook the onion and celery for about 5 minutes, until softened. Transfer to a small bowl.
Add the crab, almond flour, nutritional yeast, egg whites, mustard powder, paprika, and cloves to the bowl with the vegetables, and mix.
Place the mushroom caps on a baking sheet top down. Fill each with the crab mix, and sprinkle 1 tablespoon of the crushed rice cereal over the top.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender, and serve.
Pat the ono dry with paper towels, and put in a large resealable bag.

In a small bowl, mix well to combine the coconut oil, lime juice, garlic, cayenne pepper, and salt. Pour into the resealable bag with the fish. Seal the bag, and gently massage to ensure the fillets are well coated. Marinate in the refrigerator for 20 minutes.
Grill the ono for about 4 minutes on each side. The fish is done when it is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Serve each fillet topped with ⅔ cup of the salsa.
Preheat the broiler.
Line a baking sheet with nonstick aluminum foil, and lightly spray the foil with olive oil spray.
In a small bowl, mix the coriander, garam masala, ginger, turmeric, salt, and red pepper.
Place the fillets on the lined baking sheet, and rub the spice mixture evenly over each fillet.
Loosely cover with foil, and broil 4 to 6 inches from the flame for about 7 minutes.
Remove the foil and broil for about 3 minutes more, to desired degree of doneness.
In a small glass baking dish just big enough to hold the salmon fillets, sprinkle the fillets with salt.
In a small bowl, whisk together the vinegar, lemon juice, olive oil, and garlic. Pour the mixture over the salmon fillets.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon of the minced rosemary over the top of the fillets, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat, and lightly oil the grate.
Remove the salmon from the marinade, and discard any remaining marinade. Grill for 4 minutes on each side, until the fish is opaque in the center and flakes easily with a fork.
Transfer to a platter, sprinkle with the remaining tablespoon of minced rosemary, and serve.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Line a baking sheet with nonstick aluminum foil, and lightly coat the foil with olive oil spray.
TO MAKE THE CREMA: In a small bowl, mix together the green onions, cilantro, yogurt, olive oil, lime zest and juice, salt, and garlic, and set aside.
TO MAKE THE MAHIMAHI, step 1: In a small bowl, mix together the coriander, cumin, paprika, red pepper, salt, and garlic powder.
TO MAKE THE MAHIMAHI, step 2: Place the fillets on the prepared baking sheet. Sprinkle the spice mixture evenly over both sides of each mahimahi fillet, and pat it gently into place.
TO MAKE THE MAHIMAHI, step 3: Bake for about 10 minutes, until opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
TO ASSEMBLE THE TACOS, step 1: Heat the tortillas according to package directions.

TO ASSEMBLE THE TACOS, step 2: Place two corn tortillas on a plate, and divide one (6-ounce) fillet between them, gently breaking the fillet apart with a fork into large flakes. Top each taco with ¼ cup of cabbage and 1 tablespoon of crema. Garnish with lime wedges.
TO ASSEMBLE THE TACOS, step 3: Repeat with the remaining ingredients and serve.

method.step: Slice the cucumber into thin rounds using a mandoline slicer, or knife.
Quarter the onion, and thinly slice with a mandoline slicer, or knife.
In a large bowl, toss the cucumber, onion, and cilantro.
In a small bowl, mix the stevia, vinegar, and lime juice until the stevia is dissolved.
Add the dressing to the salad, and toss to coat.
Divide the salad among five salad plates, garnish each with about 1½ tablespoons of cashews (if using), and serve. ≈1 cup  w/o   nuts ≈1 cup   w nuts
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Place the chicken breasts on a nonstick pan, and bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through. Cooking time will vary based on the size of the breasts.
Let the chicken cool, and cut into cubes.
In a large bowl, toss the chicken, celery, and apples. In a small bowl, mix the yogurt and lemon juice. Add the yogurt mixture to the chicken mixture, and toss to coat.
Add the dates and walnuts, and toss. Season with the salt and stevia.
Put about 2 cups of the mixed greens on each of 4 large serving plates, and top each with one-quarter of the chicken mixture. Serve cold and enjoy! ≈
In a small bowl, whisk well to combine the olive oil, honey, apple cider vinegar, lemon zest and juice, brown mustard, and garlic powder, and season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, drizzle the dressing on top of the Brussels sprouts and toss well.
Add the blueberries, cranberries, and almonds, toss gently, and enjoy.
In a large bowl, gently break the salmon into large flakes with a fork.
Add the celery, onion, dill, capers, vinegar, salt (if using), and pepper, and mix well.
Divide among four plates and serve, either alone or on a bed of your favorite salad greens.
In a small bowl, mix well to combine the orange juice, apple cider vinegar, stevia, salt, pepper, and garlic.
In a medium bowl, pour the dressing over the beets and toss to coat evenly.
Put 1½ cups mixed salad greens on each plate, and top with ½ cup of the beets, the sections of 1 tangerine, and 1½ teaspoons of toasted walnuts.
Drizzle a little dressing from the bowl of beets over the top and serve.
In a large bowl, mix the kale and salt, massaging the leaves with your hands until the leaves are darker in color and fragrant, about 5 minutes.
Add the apple, radishes, cranberries, pecans, and goat cheese to the bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, water, apple cider vinegar, mustard, and honey, and season with salt and pepper. Pour the dressing over the salad, and toss to coat.
Divide among four plates and serve.
In a salad bowl, sprinkle the cherry tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil over the baby spinach.
Drizzle the olive oil and balsamic over the top, season with salt and pepper, and enjoy.
In a small bowl, mix together the vinegar, olive oil, water, oregano, garlic, mustard, salt, and pepper.
In a large bowl, toss to combine the beans, fennel, onions, olives, parsley, tomatoes, and feta. Pour the vinaigrette on top, and toss again.
Sprinkle the salad with the feta, sunflower seeds, and pepperoncini (if using). Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to allow the flavors to meld.
Serve on its own, on a bed of mixed greens, or as a side dish.

recipes.title: SOUTHWESTERN SALAD WITH PULLED CHICKEN AND CILANTRO-LIME DRESSING
recipes.author: Kendall Lou Schmidt

method.step: In a food processor or blender, process the cilantro leaves, yogurt, garlic, lime juice, olive oil, and apple cider vinegar until smooth. If too thick, add water in small increments and process to desired thickness. Refrigerate while preparing the salad.
In a large bowl, evenly spread the black beans and Pulled Chicken on top of the romaine. Sprinkle the tomatoes and avocado over the salad.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad, garnish with the salsa and cilantro leaves, and enjoy.
In a small bowl, mix together the flour, vinegar, lime juice, soy sauce, honey, garlic, ginger, salt, and red pepper flakes. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
In a large bowl, toss together the cabbage, carrots, bell pepper, green onions, and cilantro.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad, toss again, and enjoy.
In a medium saucepan over medium- high heat, heat the olive oil. Add the curry and garlic, and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the quinoa and water, and bring to a boil. Cover, reduce the heat, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until tender and no water remains.
Remove from heat, stir in the salt, and set aside to cool.
Once the quinoa has cooled completely, add the mango, celery, green onion, and cilantro. Toss gently.
In a small bowl, stir well to combine the cucumber, mint, and yogurt.
Put some spinach on each plate, top each with about ¾ cup quinoa mixture and 2 tablespoons yogurt mixture, and serve.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, stir the vegetable broth together with the vinegar and garlic. Add the Brussels sprouts, and stir gently to coat.

Line a large, rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat (or lightly spray the sheet with olive oil spray, but it will add a slight amount of fat). Spread the Brussels sprouts on the prepared sheet in a single layer. ½ cup
Sprinkle the Brussels sprouts generously with the red pepper flakes and garlic powder (if using), and season with salt. Bake for 25 to 35 minutes, until the Brussels sprouts are just tender.

Stir, sprinkle with more red pepper flakes and garlic powder (if using), and season again with salt. Bake for 15 to 25 minutes more, until the sprouts are tender when pierced with a sharp knife (cooking time will vary based on the size of the sprouts).
Transfer to a platter, plates, or meal prep containers, and serve hot or warm.

In a food processor fitted with the shredding disk, or using the large holes of a box grater, grate the zucchini. You should have 4 cups. Add the salt, and stir to mix. Transfer to a colander set over the sink, and let stand for 10 minutes.
Using your hands or a kitchen towel, squeeze the zucchini tightly to extract excess moisture (the drier the better).
Transfer the dried zucchini to a large mixing bowl, add the coconut flour, flaxseed meal, egg whites, and green onions, and mix well.
Press enough of the mixture firmly into a ½-cup measuring cup to fill the cup.

Heat half of the coconut oil in a pan with a lid large enough to fit four fritters over medium heat. Add the fritter from the measuring cup, make three more fritters, and add them to the pan. Cover, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until brown on the bottom.
Uncover, flip the fritters, cover again, and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes. The fritters should be brown on each side.
Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
In a large bowl, whisk the broth, cumin, garlic powder, nutritional yeast, salt, and lime juice until the spices are well blended and the salt is dissolved.
Add the cauliflower florets to the broth mixture, and toss to coat.

Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat (or lightly grease with extra-virgin olive oil spray, but this will add a slight amount of fat). Spread the cauliflower florets on the prepared sheet in a single layer.
Roast for 40 to 60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the florets are tender.
Transfer the florets to plates or a platter, season with more lime juice and salt, if desired, and serve hot or warm.
In a large pot, cover the potatoes with cold water, add the salt, and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, and simmer until the potatoes fall apart easily when pressed with a fork, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, whisk the 1 cup of water with ½ cup of yogurt until smooth (it should have the consistency of milk). Whisk in the olive oil, and set aside.

Drain the cooked potatoes, and transfer to a large bowl. Using a hand- held mixer on the lowest setting, or a masher, whisk, or with large fork, mash the potatoes. Gradually mix in just enough of the yogurt mixture so that the potatoes are creamy (you may not need all of the mixture).
Whisk in the remaining ½ cup of yogurt, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot. ½ cup

recipes.title: ED RED CABBAGE WITH HONEY AND MUSTARD SEEDS
recipes.author: Kendall Lou Schmidt

method.step: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat the olive oil. Add the red onion and cook, stirring often, until just softened, about 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and cook, stirring gently, until wilted, about 4 minutes.

Sprinkle the vinegar over the cabbage, and stir gently to mix. Drizzle with the honey, sprinkle with the mustard seeds, and stir to combine. Reduce the heat to medium- low and cook, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage is tender, about 10 minutes more.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve hot or warm. ½ cup
Rinse the rice in several changes of cold tap water until the water runs clear.

In a large pot fitted with a lid, bring the 2½ cups of water to a boil. Stir in the rice, lower the heat to medium, and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding more water as needed to keep the rice from scorching.
Cover the pot, remove from the heat, and let stand. You should have 3 cups of cooked rice.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat the coconut oil. Add the green onions, garlic, ginger, and red pepper flakes, and cook, stirring, for 1 minute.
Stir in the cooked rice, and cook, stirring, for 1 minute more.
Add the spinach, and cook, stirring, until the spinach is wilted and the rice is crispy around the edges, about 1 minute more.
Remove from the heat, garnish with lime juice, and serve at once.

Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat. If needed, lightly coat with olive oil spray to prevent sticking (this will add a slight amount of fat). Add the onion and garlic, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until just softened.
Add the tomatoes, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until heated through.
Add the fava beans, cumin, and cayenne pepper to the skillet. Turn the heat down to medium-low, and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Transfer the contents of the skillet to a serving bowl. Mash the fava beans with a fork to form a coarse puree, and stir in the lemon juice.
Garnish with the reserved tomato and serve.
Using a large, sharp knife, a mandoline, or a food processor fitted with the shredding disk, finely shred the cabbages and onion. Peel and grate the carrots.
In a large bowl, toss the cabbage, onion, and carrots with the salt. Let stand for at least 15 minutes, and up to 1 hour.

Transfer the cabbage mixture to a colander in the sink, and rinse thoroughly under cold running water to remove the salt. If the cabbage mixture seems soggy, transfer to a paper towel–lined baking sheet and pat dry (the less soggy the cabbage, the better the slaw).
In a large, clean bowl, whisk the apple cider vinegar, stevia, olive oil, garlic powder, pepper, and celery seeds.
Add the cabbage mixture, and toss to coat. Season with more salt, pepper, and stevia if needed, and serve.

In a large saucepan over medium- high heat, heat 1½ teaspoons of olive oil. Add the onion and garlic, and cook, stirring, for about 5 minutes, until the onion has softened and turned translucent. Stir in the quinoa.
Add 2 cups of broth, 2 teaspoons of balsamic vinegar, and 1 teaspoon of thyme.
Bring to a boil, reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for about 15 minutes, until the quinoa is tender.
Meanwhile, in a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat the remaining 1½ teaspoons of olive oil. Add the mushrooms, and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring often, until lightly browned.

Add the remaining ½ cup of vegetable broth, the remaining 4 teaspoons of balsamic vinegar, and the remaining 1 teaspoon of chopped thyme to the mushrooms, and stir to coat. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for about 5 minutes, until the mushrooms have softened.
When the quinoa has cooked, add the mushroom mixture to the saucepan and mix well.
Remove the quinoa from the heat, and immediately fold in the spinach leaves (do this quickly while the quinoa is still hot to ensure the spinach wilts completely).
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot or warm.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, toss the beets, sweet potatoes, onion, olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a foil-lined baking sheet.
Bake for 30 to 45 minutes, stirring halfway, until the sweet potatoes are tender.
Serve warm or hot.
Core the apples, and cut them into small chunks (do not peel them). The smaller the chunks, the faster the sauce will cook.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, melt the coconut oil. Add the apple chunks, and stir to coat them with the oil.
Sprinkle the apples with the water, cinnamon (if using), and lemon juice. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until the apples are tender, 10 to 15 minutes, depending on the size of your chunks.
Season with more cinnamon and stevia, if desired, and serve warm or cold.
In a small bowl, whisk the vegetable broth with the soy sauce, cornstarch, and garlic. Set the sauce aside.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat the sesame oil. Add the broccoli florets, and cook, stirring frequently, until tender, about 5 minutes.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, add the reserved sauce, and stir well to coat.
Cook for about 3 more minutes, stirring a few times, until the sauce has thickened, and serve.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat the olive oil. Add the onion and beans, and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until the onion is transparent.
Add the water, cover, and cook for 5 minutes more.
Add the apple cider vinegar, garlic, thyme, and red pepper, and mix.
Add the beets and tomato, folding them gently into the beans. Continue cooking until the beets are heated through, about 5 more minutes. Season with salt and pepper and serve.
Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Line two rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat (or lightly coat with extra-virgin olive oil spray, but this will add a slight amount of fat).
Peel the sweet potatoes, but do not rinse them (you need them dry so the oil adheres).
Using a sharp knife or a mandoline fitted with the julienne attachment, cut the sweet potatoes into ½-inch- thick fries.

Transfer the sweet potato fries to a large bowl, and drizzle in the olive oil 2 teaspoons at a time, tossing to coat. You may not need all of the oil; the fries should be evenly coated and shiny but not dripping.
Spread the fries onto the prepared baking sheets in a single layer, without crowding. No fries should be touching. Use additional baking sheets if needed.
Sprinkle the fries with the rosemary and salt, and bake for 15 minutes.
Using a spatula or tongs, flip the fries over. Continue baking for 10 to 15 minutes longer, until the fries are golden and crispy.
Divide into five equal servings, and serve warm. 3.

Using a sharp knife, cut off and discard the ends of the cucumbers. Cut off a small slice of each cucumber, and taste it for bitterness. If the cucumber tastes bitter, remove the peel. If the taste is pleasant, leave the skin on. Using a mandoline or a sharp knife, thinly slice the cucumbers (the thinner the better).
Transfer the cucumbers to a colander set in the sink, sprinkle with the 2 tablespoons of salt, and toss to coat. Let stand for at least 30 minutes to draw out excess moisture.
Meanwhile, using the mandoline or sharp knife, slice each onion quarter as thinly as possible.
Using your hands or kitchen towels, squeeze the cucumbers to remove as much moisture as possible.
In a serving bowl, toss the cucumbers and onion with the yogurt. Season with salt and pepper.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, preferably overnight or more. The longer the cucumbers marinate, the better the flavor.
Sprinkle with paprika or dill and serve.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.

Heat a medium skillet over medium- high heat, and lightly coat with olive oil spray. Add the onion, and cook for about 5 minutes, until tender. Add the kale and spinach, and cook for about 3 minutes, until the kale is tender and the spinach is wilted. Remove from the heat.

In a medium bowl, use a fork to mix the spaghetti squash, cooked vegetables, egg whites, eggs, mozzarella, nutritional yeast, salt, and black pepper until the eggs are beaten and all the ingredients are well mixed.
Lightly coat a 9-inch pie dish with olive oil spray. Pour the mixture into the pie dish, and bake for 35 minutes, until the top is golden and the eggs are firmly set.
Let rest for 10 minutes, cut into 8 slices, and serve warm. Leftovers can be stored in a tightly sealed container in the fridge for up to one week.

In a food processor or blender, blend the raspberries, almond milk, and stevia until a thick, smooth texture is formed. You will have to shake or stir the ingredients a few times. Avoid the urge to add extra almond milk. It will make the sorbet runny.
Spoon into a serving bowl and enjoy.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
In a small bowl, soak the chia seeds in the water for about 5 minutes, until they form a gel.
In a food processor or blender, blend the chia gel, avocado, cocoa powder, and vanilla until smooth.
In a large bowl, whip the egg whites and cream of tartar until stiff peaks form. Gradually add the stevia and the chia–cocoa powder mixture.
Pour into 8 ramekins or a baking- cup-lined muffin tin. Place in a water bath (a larger pan filled with water), and bake for 45 minutes.
The center will still be gooey. Transfer to the refrigerator for about 30 minutes to chill completely.
To serve, top with some fresh fruit or sprinkle with cinnamon and a little more stevia (remember to add calories from the fruit to the total). 1 dish

recipes.title: GREEK YOGURT “CHEESECAKE” WITH CHOCOLATE PROTEIN CRUMB CRUST
recipes.author: Kendall Lou Schmidt

method.step: Preheat the oven to 300°F.
In a medium bowl, mix the almond flour, whey protein, cocoa powder, flaxseed, and stevia. Gradually add the melted coconut oil, and mix until large crumbs form.
Transfer to an ungreased 8-by- 8-inch pan, spreading over the bottom and pressing the crumb mixture firmly down to form an even crust.
In a medium bowl, beat the eggs. Add the yogurt, and mix until smooth. Add the vanilla, and then gradually stir in the stevia and baking mix. Pour the mixture into the crust.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until the center is firm.
Allow to cool completely, about 30 minutes.
Cut into nine even slices and serve plain or with a sugar-free jelly (remember to add the calories from the jelly to the total).
Preheat the oven to 300°F.
In a small bowl, mix the psyllium husk, xanthan gum, and hot water. Allow the mixture to sit and thicken for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a blender or food processor, process the almond flour, almonds, cornstarch, salt, and baking soda, stopping to stir and scrape down the sides as needed, until a fine flour forms.
Add the psyllium husk mixture to the food processor, and process. If the dough is still crumbly, add 1 tablespoon of water at a time, blending between additions, until the dough clumps together.
Place the dough on a piece of parchment paper or a silicone baking sheet, and roll into a 10-inch circle.

Place the dough in a lightly greased 9-inch pie tin using this easy trick with 2 pie tins: First, place 1 pie tin upside down on your work surface. Pick up the parchment paper with the dough, and drape it dough-side-down onto the overturned pie tin. Peel off the parchment paper, and place the second pie tin over the dough. Flip the whole thing over, and remove the inner pie tin. This may seem like extra work, but it does a great job of preventing rips or tears in the dough.

In a blender or food processor, blend the pumpkin, yogurt, cottage cheese, egg whites, cinnamon, allspice, ginger, nutmeg, cloves, salt, and stevia on high for 2 to 3 minutes, until smooth. Pour the mixture over the crust.
Bake for 25 to 35 minutes, until small cracks start to form on the filling. If you gently shake the pie, the filling will still wiggle.
Remove the pie from the oven, and allow it to cool completely, about 30 minutes.
Cut into eight even slices and serve.

recipes.title: SUGAR- AND GLUTEN-FREE PEANUT BUTTER COOKIES
recipes.author: Kendall Lou Schmidt

method.step: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking sheet.
In a small bowl, mix the egg white, vanilla, and flaxseed. Set aside to rest.

If any oil has separated from the peanut butter, mix together until smooth. In a large bowl, mix the peanut butter and stevia. Add the egg white mixture, and mix until smooth with no visible stevia granules.

Scoop out about 1 tablespoon of dough, and roll it into a ball; you should have about 16 even balls. Place the balls on the prepared sheet. Using a fork, make a crosshatch by gently pressing down in one direction, then again in another, making the crisscross pattern.
Bake for 8 to 12 minutes. Less time will give a softer cookie, more time will give a crispier cookie.
Cool for a few minutes before removing the cookies from the baking sheet and serving.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
In a large bowl, mix the whey, stevia, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, baking powder, and baking soda.
In a medium bowl, stir the casein and water well. Stir in the egg whites, coconut oil, and pumpkin.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry, and mix together.
Spoon the dough onto a lightly greased cookie sheet to form about 30 cookies.
Bake for 6 to 8 minutes. Cool completely, about 15 minutes, and then use a spatula to remove from the baking sheet.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
In a small bowl, mix the psyllium husk, xanthan gum, and hot water. Set aside to thicken into a gel.
In a food processor or blender, process the almond flour, almonds, cornstarch, salt, and baking soda, stopping to stir and scrape down the sides as needed, until a fine flour forms.
Add the psyllium husk gel mixture to the food processor, and process. If the dough is still crumbly, add 1 tablespoon of water at a time, blending between additions, until the dough clumps together.
Place the dough on a piece of parchment paper or a silicone baking sheet, roll it out into a thin even rectangle, and set aside.
In a large bowl, mix the apples, cinnamon, and stevia.

Spread the apple filling on the dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges. Fold in the short edges of the rectangle. Fold the long edges in and over all the filling so that they meet in the center. Smooth out the dough to seal in the filling. It is okay to leave a short slit down the center where the dough meets to expose a small strip of filling, but try to eliminate any gaps or holes elsewhere.
Bake for 20 to 22 minutes, until the crust feels solid to the touch and the apples are bubbling through the slit. Note that the crust will not brown as it would with wheat flour.
Cool for at least 10 minutes. Cut in half down the length and into 6 down the width, forming 12 equal pieces. Store in the refrigerator for up to a week. Enjoy warm, cold, or at room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat.
In a medium bowl, whisk the egg whites until foamy.
Add the stevia, vanilla extract, and salt, and whisk well.

Put the coconut flakes in a medium bowl. Add the egg white mixture, a little at a time, to the coconut flakes. You may not need all of the mixture. You want to add just enough to hold the flakes together, but not so much that the egg white mixture is pooling in the bottom of the bowl. The macaroon mixture should feel a little sticky, making it possible to shape the macaroons.
With wet hands, make 16 balls (about the size of golf balls) from the coconut mixture, and place them on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until some of the flakes look toasted and are no longer sticky to the touch.
Cool for 5 minutes and serve or store in an airtight container for up to a week.
Preheat the oven to 300°F.
In a large bowl, whisk the egg whites and Greek yogurt. Add the stevia, and mix well.

In a small microwave-safe bowl, heat the key lime juice in the microwave for 1½ to 2 minutes, until very hot. Stir in the xanthan gum, and mix until it dissolves completely. As the mixture cools, it should start to thicken. Once the key lime mixture is cool to touch, add it to the Greek yogurt mixture and stir.
Gradually add the cornstarch, mixing thoroughly between additions. Set the filling aside.
In a small bowl, mix the flaxseed with the water, and set aside to thicken.
In a large bowl, mix the protein powder, stevia, almond flour, and cinnamon.
Gradually add the flaxseed mixture, and knead into a dough.
Lightly coat a pie tin with olive oil spray, and press the dough into the pie tin.
Pour the filling on top of the crust. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until the center is set and does not wiggle when you shake the pie tin and the top has browned slightly.
Transfer to the refrigerator to cool, about 30 minutes.
Cut into eight equal slices and serve cold.
In a large bowl, mix the yogurt, whey protein powder, and pineapple.
In a small microwaveable bowl, microwave the water for 5 minutes, or boil on the stove top. Immediately add the Jell-O, and stir until the powder is completely dissolved.
Stir the Jell-O into the yogurt mixture.

Refrigerate until solid, 4 hours and up to overnight. If you like, before refrigerating, transfer the mixture into a Jell-O mold that has been lightly coated with olive oil spray (this will add a slightly amount of fat). If using a mold, invert it, remove the center piece to release the Jell-O, and remove the lid.
Serve plain or topped with additional crushed pineapple (remember to add the extra calories to the total).

method.step: Preheat the oven to 350°F.

In a food processor or blender, process the black beans, protein powder, honey, coconut oil, cocoa powder, stevia, vanilla extract, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt until very smooth. Fold in the chocolate chips using a spoon.
Lightly coat an 8-by-8-inch baking dish with olive oil spray, and transfer the batter to the baking dish.
Bake for 15 minutes (the center may still seem a bit undone), and refrigerate immediately for 15 minutes to cool and set.
Cut into 8 bars, each about  4 by 2 inches, and serve or store covered in the refrigerator for  up to a week.

recipes.title: CHOCOLATE PROTEIN MUG CAKE WITH WHIPPED PEANUT BUTTER FROSTING
recipes.author: Kendall Lou Schmidt

method.step: In a large mug, mix the casein, flaxseed, and water, and set aside to thicken for about 1 minute.
Add the egg whites, vanilla, whey, cocoa powder, stevia, baking soda, and cinnamon, and mix well.
Microwave in the mug for 2 to 3 minutes, depending on the depth of the cup. Keep an eye on it to prevent burning or drying out.
Cool completely, about 15 minutes, and then flip the cake over onto a plate.
In a small bowl mix the Cool Whip Lite, flour, stevia, vanilla, and yogurt (if using) until smooth.
Spread the frosting onto the cake, cut into four even pieces, and serve.
In a blender, blend the protein powder, flaxseed, cinnamon, vanilla, water, and ice until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the almonds, almond milk, banana, oatmeal, whey protein, and ice until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the protein powder, water, yogurt, berries, stevia, and ice (if using) until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the coffee, casein, stevia, cinnamon, nutmeg, pumpkin extract, and ice until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the casein, spinach, pineapple, water, coconut milk, stevia, and ice (if using) until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a shaker cup or blender, shake or blend the almond milk, protein powder, stevia, cinnamon, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the casein, peaches, water, stevia, and ice (if using) until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the spinach, water, egg whites, orange, apple, ginger, and ice until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the casein, strawberries, water, yogurt, and stevia until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the water, protein powder, peanut butter, stevia, and hazelnut extract until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the blueberries, beets, protein powder, chia seeds, honey, and ice (if using) until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the cashews, casein, oats, honey, cinnamon, water, and ice until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the almond milk, casein, cashews, date, root beer extract, and ice until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the blueberries, casein, oats, flaxseed, psyllium, stevia, water, and ice (if using) until smooth.
Pour into a glass and serve.
In a blender, blend the protein powder, casein, orange juice, coconut milk, stevia, and ice until smooth.
Pour into a glass and enjoy.
In a blender, blend the egg whites, raspberries, orange juice, stevia, and ice (if using) until smooth.
Pour into a glass and serve.
In a food processor or blender, process the whey protein, cashews, almond flour, and cinnamon until a flour consistency is reached. Transfer to a large bowl.
Pour the IMO syrup over the dry ingredients. Using a spoon, mix until a thick, sticky batter forms and the batter is well mixed.
Using your hands, form the batter into 4 evenly sized bars and place them in individual resealable bags. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, until firm.
Store for up to 1 week in the refrigerator or 1 month in the freezer.
Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Lightly coat a baking sheet with olive oil spray.
In a large bowl, mix the oats, crisp rice cereal, almonds, macadamia nuts, coconut, and pineapple. Set aside.
In a small saucepan over medium- low heat, melt the coconut oil. Whisk in the honey and almond milk until smooth. Whisk in the protein powder until smooth.
Stir the protein mixture into the oat and rice cereal mixture.
Using wet hands, press the mixture firmly into 10 evenly sized bars, about 4 by 2 inches each, and place them on the prepared sheet.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the bars start to turn golden.
Let cool for 15 minutes, and then transfer to a storage container or resealable bags. Store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week or the freezer for up to 1 month.
Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Lightly coat a baking sheet with olive oil spray.
In a large bowl, mix the oats, walnuts, cranberries, and cinnamon. Set aside.
In a small saucepan over medium- low heat, heat the coconut oil. Whisk in the maple syrup, honey, and almond milk until smooth. Whisk in the protein powder until smooth.

Add the protein mixture to the oat mixture, and stir well. Transfer to the prepared baking sheet. Using wet hands, press the mixture firmly into 10 evenly sized bars. Bars can be rectangular, or you can form balls and press them flat like a cookie.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the bars start to turn golden.
Let cool for 10 minutes, and then transfer to a storage container or resealable bags. Store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week or in the freezer for up to 1 month.
In a large bowl, mix the oat flour, peanut flour, crisp rice cereal, and salt.
Add the peanut butter, maple syrup, and vanilla, and stir until it resembles a cookie dough.
Using your hands, roll the batter into 10 evenly sized balls. Freeze for 5 to 10 minutes.
Remove from the freezer, and transfer to resealable bags or a storage container. Store in the refrigerator for 1 week or in the freezer for up to 1 month.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking sheet.
In a large bowl, mix the oat flour, psyllium husk, protein powder, and crisp rice cereal.
Add the almond butter and honey. Mix until crumbly clumps form.

Using your hands, gather the batter into a ball. Transfer to the prepared baking sheet. Using your hands to press or a rolling pin, make a rectangle. Freeze for 5 to 10 minutes, or if it will not fit in the freezer, refrigerate for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cut into 10 evenly sized bars, and transfer to resealable bags or a storage container. Store in the refrigerator for 1 week or in the freezer for up to 1 month.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a food processor or blender, process the oat flour, protein powder, and cocoa powder until well mixed.
Add the dates, ½ cup of walnuts, and the vanilla, salt, and cinnamon. Process until a thick dough forms.

Transfer the dough to the prepared baking sheet. Using your hands, knead in the remaining ¼ cup of walnuts and the chocolate chips, and then shape the dough into a square. A larger square will result in thinner bars.
Gently cut into 10 evenly sized bars, and transfer to resealable bags or an airtight storage container. Store for up to 1 week in the refrigerator or 1 month in the freezer.
Line a baking sheet with plastic wrap or parchment paper.
In a food processor or blender, pulse the walnuts, pecans, cinnamon, and salt a few times, until the nuts are chopped into large pieces.
Add the dates and apple, a few at time, pulsing between additions. Once all the dates and apple have been added, process until you have a thick mixture that sticks together.

Spoon the mixture onto the prepared baking sheet, and using your hands, form an 8-inch square. Cover with a second piece of plastic wrap or parchment paper. (For presentation, if you prefer, you can use a roller to smooth out the mixture.)
Refrigerate for 30 minutes or more.
Cut into 8 bars, each about 4 by 2 inches. Wrap the bars in plastic wrap or transfer to individual resealable bags so they don’t stick together. Store in the refrigerator for up to a few weeks.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, mix the oat flour, rolled oats, protein powder, and crisp rice cereal. Set aside.
In a small saucepan over medium- low heat, stir the honey, peanut butter, and vanilla until smooth.
Stir the peanut butter mixture into the oat mixture.
Add the water 1 tablespoon at a time, stirring after each addition, until a thick batter forms. You may not need all the water.
Transfer the dough to the prepared baking sheet. Using your hands, shape the dough into a square. A larger square will result in thinner bars.
In a small microwavable bowl, melt the chocolate chips in the microwave on high for 1 minute. Using a spoon, drizzle the melted chocolate over the dough, or spread it out over all.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Cut into 10 evenly sized squares, and transfer to resealable bags or a storage container. Store for up to 1 week in the refrigerator or 1 month in the freezer.
Line a baking sheet with plastic wrap or parchment paper.
In a food processor or blender, pulse the almonds, cashews, cinnamon, salt, and vanilla a few times, until the nuts are chopped into large pieces.
Add the dates a few at a time, processing after each addition. Once all the dates have been added, process until you have a thick mixture that sticks together.

Spoon the mixture onto the prepared baking sheet, and using your hands, form an 8-inch square. Cover with a second piece of plastic wrap or parchment paper. (For presentation, if you prefer, you can use a roller to smooth out the mixture.)
Refrigerate for 30 minutes or more.

Cut into 8 evenly sized bars, each about 4 by 2 inches. Wrap the bars in plastic wrap or transfer to individual resealable bags so they don’t stick together. Store the bars in the refrigerator for up to a few weeks.
Line a baking sheet with plastic wrap or parchment paper.
In a food processor or blender, pulse the almonds, cashews, and shredded coconut a few times, until the nuts are chopped into large pieces.
With the food processor running, add the vanilla extract and dates. Process until you have a thick mixture that sticks together.

Spoon the mixture onto the prepared baking sheet, and using your hands, form the mixture into an 8-inch square. Cover with a second piece of plastic wrap or parchment paper. (For presentation, if you prefer, you can use a roller to smooth out the mixture.)
Refrigerate for 30 minutes or more.

Cut into 8 bars, each about 4 by 2 inches. Wrap the bars in plastic wrap or transfer to individual resealable bags so they don’t stick together. Store the bars in the refrigerator for up to a few weeks, or in the freezer for a few months.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat.
In a medium bowl, stir the protein powder and 6 tablespoons of almond flour together with the coconut flour and stevia.
Add the raspberries and vanilla extract. Using a fork, stir until a thick, sticky dough forms.

Lightly dust the prepared baking sheet with the remaining 2 tablespoons of almond flour. Transfer the dough to the baking sheet, and roll it around so that it is very lightly coated with just enough almond flour to make it no longer sticky. Using your hands, shape it into a long, narrow rectangle, about 10 by 2 inches. Using a butter knife, cut the dough into 5 pieces, each 2 by 2 inches.
In a small microwavable bowl, melt the chocolate in the microwave for 1 to 2 minutes. Dip each square of the dough into the chocolate to lightly coat, and place back on the baking sheet.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes, until the chocolate hardens.
Transfer to a storage container or resealable bags, and store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
Line a baking sheet with plastic wrap or parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, mix the banana and almond flour until well- incorporated but crumbly.
In a small saucepan over medium- low heat, stir the cashew butter and protein until melted and smooth. Stir into the banana mixture until well- incorporated and a thick batter forms.

Spoon the mixture onto the prepared baking sheet, and using your hands, form the mixture into an 8-inch square. Cover with a second piece of plastic wrap or parchment paper. (For presentation, if you prefer, you can use a roller to smooth out the mixture.)
Refrigerate for 15 minutes, until firm.
Cut into eight evenly sized squares, and transfer to storage containers or resealable bags. Store for up to 1 week in the refrigerator or 1 month in the freezer.
In a food processor or blender, process the whey protein, cashews, almond flour, and lemon zest until well-mixed. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Sir in the lemon juice gradually, mixing until a thick dough forms.
Using your hands, form the batter into four balls. Place them on a plate and flatten into cookies. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes, until firm.
Transfer to a storage container or resealable bag, and store for up to 1 week in the refrigerator or 1 month in the freezer.

Using wet hands, form the batter into four evenly sized bars and place them in individual resealable bags. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, until firm.
Store for up to 1 week in the refrigerator or 1 month in the freezer.
In a food processor or blender, process the whey protein, cashews, almond flour, and ¼ cup of dried strawberries until a flour is reached. Transfer to a large bowl.
Pour the IMO syrup over the dry ingredients. Using a spoon, mix until a thick, sticky batter forms. Add the remaining ¼ cup of dried strawberries, and using your hands, knead until well mixed.
Using your hands, form the batter into four evenly sized bars and place them in individual resealable bags. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, until firm.
Store for up to 1 week in the refrigerator or 1 month in the freezer.
Blend all the paste ingredients in a food processor.
Heat the oil in a saucepan or wok and fry the paste over low heat till fragrant (approximately 5-6 mins).
Add coconut milk and lemongrass into the wok and continue stirring.
Add beef, kaffir lime leaves and turmeric leaves and bring the coconut milk and paste to boil over medium heat.
Bring to simmer over a low heat and add water from time to time to prevent the dish from drying out. Remember to continue stirring often to prevent burning.
In a separate pan, dry-fry the grated coconut until golden brown and transfer into a pestle and mortar to turn into a paste.

method.step: Add the coconut paste and cook till the beef turns dark brown and when the meat has absorbed all the spices and flavours. The process should take about 3 hours.
Serve with jasmine rice or bread.
